goal: T-KRP-C: Builder agent posture: surgical changes + simplicity-first enforcement
limitations: External upstream repository shape and vendor instruction surfaces are time-sensitive and were checked during the 2026-04-23 dynamic-full-auto planning repair.
This capsule is planning evidence for hydrating T-KRP-C into backlog/spec state. It does not authorize editing builder agent posture files without a later governed M1 delivery scope.
T-KRP-C should stay builder-specific: do not implement orchestrator goal-classification checkpoints reserved for T-KRP-D or structured-autonomy success gates reserved for T-KRP-E.
Generated builder mirrors should not be manually edited. If a later implementation changes canonical builder posture, generated surfaces must be refreshed through scripts/azoth-deploy.py.
The upstream Karpathy guidelines inform acceptance criteria, but Azoth must keep repo-native governance, staged handoffs, deploy parity, and validation expectations.

thesis: T-KRP-C should make the Builder agent's later implementation posture explicitly enforce small, goal-traceable, simplicity-first changes with narrow verification. The planning repair should create only backlog/spec/research state; the future governed delivery should edit canonical builder posture and regenerate mirrors through the deploy path.

upstream_guidelines.implication: Builder posture should require the minimum change that solves the task, avoid speculative abstractions, preserve unrelated code, and report verification evidence.

industry_review_practice.small_changes: Google engineering guidance favors small, focused changes because they are easier and faster to review and less risky to roll back.
industry_review_practice.pull_request_focus: Microsoft engineering playbook guidance emphasizes focused pull requests with clear evidence and reviewability.
industry_review_practice.code_review_surface: GitHub pull request review mechanics reinforce that changed files and conversations are the review surface; builder reports should make changed paths and residual risk explicit.

agent_vendor_context.openai_codex: Codex guidance around repo instructions and checks supports keeping builder behavior tied to local instructions and verifiable commands.
agent_vendor_context.anthropic_claude_code: Claude Code best-practice guidance supports explicit context, planning, and verification rather than broad ungrounded edits.

planned_task.title: Builder agent posture: surgical changes + simplicity-first enforcement

existing_boundaries: T-KRP-A owns root CLAUDE.md always-on behavioral guidance.
T-KRP-B owns the dedicated karpathy-principles skill.
T-KRP-C owns builder agent posture only.
T-KRP-D owns orchestrator assumption-surfacing at goal classification.
canonical_builder_surface: agents/tier1-core/builder.agent.md is the likely authored builder source.
.claude/agents/builder.md and .codex/agents/builder.toml are generated or platform-projected surfaces and should not be manually edited in the planning repair.

spec_direction.intent: Hydrate a governed M1 task for refining Builder posture around surgical changes, simplicity-first implementation, and goal-driven verification.
scope: Refine the canonical Builder agent posture so implementation stages state owned surfaces before editing and keep changes traceable to the approved goal.
Require Builder to prefer existing repo patterns and helpers over new abstractions unless the abstraction removes real repeated complexity.
Require Builder to avoid drive-by cleanup and preserve unrelated dirty state.
Require Builder final reports to name changed paths, goal mapping, validation commands, outcomes, and residual risk.
Regenerate generated builder mirrors only through scripts/azoth-deploy.py if the future implementation touches canonical builder posture.
non_goals: No manual edits to generated builder mirrors.
No hook-level enforcement in the initial T-KRP-C implementation unless explicitly re-scoped.
No broad rewrite of all agent archetypes.
acceptance: The future governed implementation updates the canonical builder posture with explicit simplicity-first and surgical-change constraints.
Builder guidance includes a pre-edit scope statement and a final verification/reporting checklist.
Generated mirrors are refreshed via scripts/azoth-deploy.py if affected.
Acceptance keeps T-KRP-D and T-KRP-E explicitly deferred.
Validation includes deploy parity checks and targeted tests for generated agent surfaces.

commands: PYTHONPATH=scripts python3 -m pytest tests/test_agents.py tests/test_azoth_deploy.py tests/test_codex_adapter_templates.py -q
integration_expectations: Canonical builder source changes must project to enabled platform mirrors.
Generated mirrors must be refreshed through azoth-deploy rather than manually edited.
Future builder-stage summaries should expose scope traceability, verification evidence, and residual risk.
